{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Reuse Spring XD's existing module/plugin architecture for U1, U2, U5, and U6 rather than building parallel infrastructure.",
    "Design a codec SPI (Service Provider Interface) for U1 so that encoders/decoders can be registered per-stream and swapped at runtime via module options.",
    "For U2, implement gpfdist sink as a native XD module that streams records over the gpfdist external table protocol using an embedded gpfdist-compatible HTTP server (or client to an external gpfdist instance).",
    "For U3, select a lightweight SPA-style front-end stack and a REST/WS admin backend; the UI infrastructure must be modular so admin_ui and Flo can plug in their own views without duplication.",
    "For U5, choose the Spring Batch tasklet approach over the streaming/messaging approach for whole-file ingestion, because it avoids holding file contents in memory and removes bus overhead.",
    "For U6, implement gpload tasklet by shelling out to the gpload utility with a generated control file, since gpload is the officially supported high-throughput loader for GPDB/HAWQ.",
    "For U7, change the Spring XD launcher script/manifest to relocate Hadoop jars from the root classloader to an isolated child classloader that is only instantiated when an HDFS-backed module registry is configured.",
    "For U8, define a classpath resolver DSL that supports glob patterns, ${xd.home} placeholders, per-distro subdirectories, and per-module property substitution evaluated at module deployment time.",
    "Adopt a single code branch / shared module-loader component for U7 and U8 to avoid duplicate classpath management logic.",
    "Use JUnit and Spring XD's existing integration test harness for verification; do not introduce new test frameworks."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The target project is Spring XD (not core Spring Framework); the surrounding prose about Spring Framework is treated as background context.",
    "A single developer performs all work; estimates reflect hand-on-keyboard coding plus design and test effort, but exclude meetings, code reviews by others, and release management.",
    "Java 8+ toolchain is available and the existing XD build (Gradle) and module SPI are stable baselines.",
    "GPDB/HAWQ, Kafka, and Hadoop distributions (e.g., PHD22) are available in a local dev/test environment for the gpfdist, Kafka, and classpath work.",
    "UI work for U3 is greenfield within the XD ecosystem: there is no existing shared admin shell to extend, so a thin shell + plugin slots is built first.",
    "gpfdist and gpload binaries are assumed to be installable on the target hosts and reachable from XD containers; integration with those binaries, not the internals of GPDB, is in scope.",
    "Dynamic classpath changes in U8 only need to apply to module-level dependencies, not to XD's own runtime classloader; OSGi-style live reloading is out of scope.",
    "The end-to-end Kafka use case (U4) targets demonstration/benchmark fidelity rather than production hardening, so a single representative topology is sufficient.",
    "Documentation effort is limited to module-level README/Javadoc; no full user guide is included."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A0",
      "activity_name": "Overall architecture and design",
      "activity_description": "Review existing XD module SPI, Kafka binding, admin server, and launcher; produce a short design note covering the codec SPI (U1), gpfdist/gpload module contracts (U2/U6), UI shell (U3), tasklet refactor (U5), and classloader isolation strategy (U7/U8).",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "U1 - Pluggable encoders/decoders for Kafka source, sink and bus",
      "activity_description": "Introduce an Encoder/Decoder SPI, add module-option-driven codec selection for the Kafka source, Kafka sink, and message-bus bindings, and provide a default codec so existing deployments are unaffected.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "U2 - OOTB gpfdist sink module for GPDB/HAWQ",
      "activity_description": "Create a new XD sink module that writes to a gpfdist external table (embedded or external gpfdist), supports batching, and exposes standard sink options for target table, segment column, etc.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "U3 - UI infrastructure for admin_ui and Flo integration",
      "activity_description": "Stand up a thin admin UI shell (asset pipeline, routing, layout, auth hook), expose the required REST/WS endpoints from the XD admin server, and provide registration points so admin_ui and Flo can mount their own views.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "U4 - End-to-end Kafka use case",
      "activity_description": "Build a representative source | kafka | ... | sink topology (with the new U1 codecs), add container/compose-based test harness, capture throughput/latency figures, and document the demo steps.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "U5 - Tasklet-based efficient file reading",
      "activity_description": "Refactor the file ingestion job to use a Spring Batch tasklet that streams chunks to the writer without retaining the full file in memory or sending the payload over the message bus, plus a small comparison benchmark against the stream-based path.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "U6 - gpload tasklet for GPDB ingestion",
      "activity_description": "Create a Spring Batch tasklet that prepares a staging area, generates a gpload control file from job parameters, invokes the gpload binary, captures exit status/logs, and surfaces failures through the XD job execution model.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "U7 - Remove Hadoop from root classpath",
      "activity_description": "Move Hadoop client jars out of the XD root classloader, introduce an isolated child classloader triggered only when the HDFS module registry is enabled, and update the launcher/manifest accordingly. Verify startup time and that non-HDFS paths are unaffected.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "U8 - Dynamic classpath for modules",
      "activity_description": "Extend the module loader to resolve a module.classpath option supporting globs, ${xd.home}, and ${distro} placeholders, and to add external classpath entries contributed via module options. Ensure it composes correctly with the U7 isolated classloader.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Integration testing across all user stories",
      "activity_description": "End-to-end tests covering Kafka encode/decode round-trips (U1), gpfdist/gpload loads against a live GPDB (U2/U6), UI shell serving admin_ui and Flo placeholders (U3), Kafka demo (U4), tasklet vs stream file ingestion (U5), and classpath isolation/expansion scenarios (U7/U8).",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Documentation",
      "activity_description": "Module READMEs and Javadoc for the new gpfdist sink, gpload tasklet, codec SPI, dynamic classpath option, and UI extension points, plus an updated admin UI integration note.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 304
  }
}

Design a codec SPI (Service Provider Interface) for U1 so that encoders/decoders can be registered per-stream and swapped at runtime via module options.

For U2, implement gpfdist sink as a native XD module that streams records over the gpfdist external table protocol using an embedded gpfdist-compatible HTTP server (or client to an external gpfdist instance).
For U3, select a lightweight SPA-style front-end stack and a REST/WS admin backend; the UI infrastructure must be modular so admin_ui and Flo can plug in their own views without duplication.
For U5, choose the Spring Batch tasklet approach over the streaming/messaging approach for whole-file ingestion, because it avoids holding file contents in memory and removes bus overhead.
For U6, implement gpload tasklet by shelling out to the gpload utility with a generated control file, since gpload is the officially supported high-throughput loader for GPDB/HAWQ.

For U7, change the Spring XD launcher script/manifest to relocate Hadoop jars from the root classloader to an isolated child classloader that is only instantiated when an HDFS-backed module registry is configured.
For U8, define a classpath resolver DSL that supports glob patterns, ${xd.home} placeholders, per-distro subdirectories, and per-module property substitution evaluated at module deployment time.
Adopt a single code branch / shared module-loader component for U7 and U8 to avoid duplicate classpath management logic.
Use JUnit and Spring XD's existing integration test harness for verification; do not introduce new test frameworks.
assumptions: The target project is Spring XD (not core Spring Framework); the surrounding prose about Spring Framework is treated as background context.
A single developer performs all work; estimates reflect hand-on-keyboard coding plus design and test effort, but exclude meetings, code reviews by others, and release management.
Java 8+ toolchain is available and the existing XD build (Gradle) and module SPI are stable baselines.
GPDB/HAWQ, Kafka, and Hadoop distributions (e.g., PHD22) are available in a local dev/test environment for the gpfdist, Kafka, and classpath work.
UI work for U3 is greenfield within the XD ecosystem: there is no existing shared admin shell to extend, so a thin shell + plugin slots is built first.
gpfdist and gpload binaries are assumed to be installable on the target hosts and reachable from XD containers; integration with those binaries, not the internals of GPDB, is in scope.
Dynamic classpath changes in U8 only need to apply to module-level dependencies, not to XD's own runtime classloader; OSGi-style live reloading is out of scope.
The end-to-end Kafka use case (U4) targets demonstration/benchmark fidelity rather than production hardening, so a single representative topology is sufficient.
Documentation effort is limited to module-level README/Javadoc; no full user guide is included.
